fact: President Mnangagwa said the Zimbabwe Centre for High Performance Computing (ZCHPC) national HPC data center at the University of Zimbabwe, run by ZCHPC as custodian of national HPC infrastructure, already hosts the Ministry of Health and Child Care's Impilo Electronic Health Records and Telemedicine platform, and the Civil Registry is integrated with it (date is the commissioning of Phase 2, 2025-08-15, as the article gives no other).

fact: POTRAZ, as the designated Data Protection Authority, states in its implementation guidelines that it will not permit highly sensitive information such as core banking platforms and critical financial systems to be hosted outside Zimbabwe and that such systems must be hosted locally; the document gives no date, so its published date of 2025-01-01 is used.
system: POTRAZ Data Protection Authority Implementation Guidelines (cross-border data transfers, sensitive information)

fact: Minister Mavetera announced a Zimbabwe Government Cloud and proposed a Data Sovereignty Statutory Instrument requiring all critical government data to be hosted within Zimbabwe's borders.
system: Zimbabwe Government Cloud; Data Sovereignty Statutory Instrument

fact: Deputy ICT Minister Dingumuzi Phuti said the government is mooting expansion of the National Data Centre to at least Tier four, framed as keeping Zimbabwean data processed, stored and protected locally.

ICT Minister Tatenda Mavetera said Zimbabwe is upgrading its national cloud infrastructure and will establish a new Tier 4 national data centre with the e-Government Technology Unit, targeted for completion by end 2025.
system: National cloud upgrade and new national data centre

fact: Government digital platforms including email and ministry websites run on the government's national cloud and data centre infrastructure, with the Government Internet Service Provider hosting ministry websites, according to the ICT Minister.
